about.text: Political candidates, including judicial candidates, have broad free-speech rights to “speak in support of their campaigns.” Williams-Yulee v. The Florida Bar, 575 U.S. 433, 457 (2015). But that right does not divest a duly elected government of its power to control certain speech by its confidential and policymaking employees.
